# The tests that fail on a GitHub-hosted runner and pass on every lane's machine.
#
# **One line, added 2026-10-22. It was empty before that, and had reached zero by
# being satisfied** — the note below is the history of how.
#
# `gate.yml` reads this file to tell **a failure this runner causes** from **a failure
# in the change under test**. Until it existed the workflow could only ask *which gate
# failed*, and answered `the workspace's tests` in both cases — so a real broken test
# and a namespace the runner would not make were the same sentence, and the run stayed
# quiet about both.
#
# # What was here, and why it is not
#
# Five tests: four in `alo-asking::an_office_that_cannot_connect_still_has_working_ai`
# and one in `alo-nearby::asked_and_answered_over_ipv6`. All five re-run their own test
# binary inside `unshare --map-root-user --net`, and all five failed here with **126** —
# util-linux's *found, but could not be executed*.
#
# The cause was one bit. `/home/runner` is `drwxr-x---` owned by uid 1001, and
# `--map-root-user` maps uid 0 and nothing else — so a process in that namespace holds
# no capability over it, `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` stops covering for a mode that would
# otherwise deny, and `0750` grants others nothing. **Traversal was denied to root
# itself.** The job now grants `o+x` on that directory before the gates run, and the
# five execute. Measured on 2026-09-30: zero `FAIL` lines in the whole suite, and the
# probe's `exec inside a namespace, as root: exit 0`.
#
# **The file is kept rather than deleted.** A list that reached zero by being satisfied
# is worth keeping as a list: it is the shape the next quarantine goes in, it carries
# the rules below, and its emptiness is a claim the run checks on every pass rather than
# a fact nobody revisits.
#
# # The rules a line here lives under
#
# **A line here is an excuse, so it expires.** The workflow checks not only that every
# failure is listed, but that every listed test *still fails*. A test named here that
# does not fail makes the run say so, and is meant to be deleted in the next change —
# otherwise this becomes a list of things nobody is allowed to break, which is the
# opposite of what it is for.
#
# That check had a gap of its own, found while fixing the five: when **every** gate
# passed, the deciding step returned before comparing, so the lines would have gone
# unreported by the very success that made them stale. The branch had never been green,
# so the bypass could not have been seen until the moment it began to lie.
#
# **A line is a statement about the runner, never about the test.** Nothing here is
# skipped, marked `#[ignore]`, or weakened. These tests run on every lane and must pass
# there; `alo/nine-gates` — the status `main` actually requires — is posted only from a
# machine where all of them ran.
#
# **Adding a line is not a way to land a red test.** A failure that is not already
# understood and reproduced does not belong here. Each line names what was measured and
# the exit code it produces, so a reader can check the claim.
#
# Format: one test per line, exactly as nextest names it in a FAIL line —
# `<crate>::<binary> <test>`. Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored.

# **The runner runs as root, and this test's control says root is the wrong
# question.** `crates/alo-as-it-was/src/removing.rs` exists because
# `std::fs::remove_dir_all` will not descend a directory `cp` left at mode `000`
# — which is what it leaves when a copy out of an unreadable place fails. The
# test sets a tree to `000`, asserts **the ordinary remover cannot** (its
# control), then asserts this crate's can.
#
# Measured on the gate's runner, 2026-10-22: the control fired with *if the
# ordinary remover can do this, this file has no reason to exist.* That is the
# control doing its job — **root ignores a mode**, so `remove_dir_all` succeeded
# and the premise the test is about does not hold there. Exit code of the gates
# step: 1; the `FAIL` line is the one below, verbatim.
#
# **A line is a statement about the runner, never about the test**, and this is
# exactly that: the test is right, it passes on every lane's machine as the
# person, and the one thing it needs is not being root. Dropping its control
# instead would leave a test that passes on the runner **while measuring
# nothing**, which is the trade this file exists to refuse.
#
# Its sibling in the same crate was *not* put here. It provoked the same refusal
# with a permission, and it was rewritten to provoke it by the place being let go
# of between the plan and the act — a real race that denies root exactly as it
# denies anybody. **Where a cause can be made independent of who runs it, that is
# the fix and this list is not.**
alo-as-it-was removing::tests::a_directory_with_no_permissions_is_removed
